title: Intercepting Routes for Modal Experiences
summary: Show a route as a modal during in-app navigation while keeping a full page address.

subtopics.title: Define interception boundaries
subtopics.explanation: Next.js route conventions such as `(.)` and `(..)` describe which route a folder intercepts. The number of dot segments is relative to the current route level, not a URL string. Sketch the route tree first; this makes modal routing easier to reason about than guessing the folder name.

subtopics.title: Render parallel route slots
subtopics.explanation: Parallel routes use named slots, often folders that start with `@`, to render multiple parts of a layout at once. A slot can hold a modal while the main slot shows the page. Each slot still needs sensible loading and fallback behavior when a route is not matched.

subtopics.title: Support direct page loads
subtopics.explanation: A modal opened by client navigation may be intercepted, while opening its URL directly should usually show the full page. That gives a copied link a complete destination. Test both navigation paths and provide a route fallback for the initial server request.

subtopics.title: Preserve browser history behavior
subtopics.explanation: When a modal route is opened through navigation, the Back button should return to the previous page and close the modal. Forward should reopen it when appropriate. Use Next.js navigation so the router can keep URL, history, and rendered state in sync.

subtopics.title: Make the modal accessible
subtopics.explanation: An intercepted route that looks like a modal still needs dialog behavior: an accessible name, predictable focus, a close control, and a clear dismissal path. Return focus to the opener when possible. The URL and browser history should also make the open state understandable and shareable.

foundations.overview: Intercepting routes let Next.js render a route in a different part of the route tree during client navigation. A photo can open as a modal from a gallery, while direct navigation still shows a full page. Route structure and parallel slots must be planned carefully.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like opening a book detail card over the shelf while keeping the book’s full page address.
foundations.whyItMatters: The URL remains shareable while the interface preserves the user’s place.

keyTakeaways: Parallel routes can render multiple route slots.
Direct loads should have a useful full-page experience.
Browser back should close the modal when appropriate.
Provide accessible focus and dismissal behavior.
